topics.topic: Atomic ordering of owner requests against expiry cleanup or sign-out
questions: What happens when a request passes the session check, then waits for the locks, and a sign-out or expiry pass acquires those locks first and removes the session or its uploaded file?

How is an ordinary request's arrival made atomic against the expiry pass, and which wins when the request arrives before the limit but the pass acquires the session lock before the request records that arrival?

May the expiry pass end and clear a session while an already-admitted request is using or changing its confirmation or upload, or must it wait for that request's session/import locks and apply cleanup afterward?

What happens when an upload, confirmation-step request, or other session-state request passes the session check before a limit, but the expiry pass acquires the import and session locks first and ends that session?

judgement.why: The same atomic-ordering question for admitted owner requests, expiry, sign-out and import/session locks was already judged on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Reservation and ordering of admitted requests against expiry, sign-out, and imports
quotes:
A sign-out is applied in turn with the session's other requests that
   change it: one admitted before it completes its change to the store, and
   leaves nothing in the ended session.
precedent.why: A request admitted before sign-out completes its store change even if it acquires the session lock later, while no state remains in the ended session.

topics.topic: Backup encryption, authentication, key digest, nonce, and metadata binding
questions: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce construction, key interpretation, metadata encoding and key-digest algorithm define a valid backup and detect ciphertext or header tampering?
What exact cryptographic format and algorithms make a backup encrypted, authenticated, decryptable, and associated with the recorded key digest?
Must the unencrypted instant, release, sequence number, and key digest be cryptographically bound to the ciphertext, and which mismatches make the backup fail?

Which authenticated-encryption construction, key derivation or key-length rule, nonce generation rule, key-digest algorithm, and authentication coverage are required? In particular, is the readable metadata authenticated against the encrypted store?

judgement.why: The same question about authenticated backup encryption, nonces, key identification and metadata coverage was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Authenticated backup encryption format, nonce rules, and key identification
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Backup filename namespaces, kept-name construction, and record framing
questions: What are the exact prefixes and the exact collision-free encoding of an instant into a kept filename?
What exact file names and record format must all implementations use, and how are collisions between probes, encrypted temporaries, decrypted temporaries, and kept backups prevented?

What are the two prefixes, the exact kept-name construction and timestamp precision, the metadata framing and types, the release identifier format, and the conditions under which each metadata value counts as readable and valid?

judgement.why: The same question about backup filename construction, timestamp encoding, framing and collisions was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Backup filename formats, timestamps, temporary names, and collision handling
quotes:
Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release
   declares, neither beginning with the other;

A kept
   name is made from the backup's instant and is never overwritten: a backup
   whose kept name exists, or whose rename fails, is deleted and the run
   fails.
precedent.why: The prefixes, timestamp encoding and filename grammar are backup-format encodings owned by State 6; the texts already state that an existing kept name makes the new run fail without overwriting it.

topics.topic: Configuration variable names and general well-formedness rules
questions: What is the exact environment-variable name for each store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential and service token?
What exact syntax, encoding and allowed value set makes each configuration item well formed, including how environment text is converted to the byte length used for secrets?
Which exact `REGISTRY_` names are accepted, so that Registry can distinguish required, optional-token, and unknown items?
What exact syntax, encoding, forbidden values, and path forms make each configuration item well formed?
What are the exact environment-variable names and the well-formedness rules for each store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential, and service token?

judgement.why: The same question about configuration variable names, schema and encoded well-formedness rules was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Configuration variable names and overall schema
quotes:
The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says; no other variable is read or
   checked. It holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 9).

A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start; Registry applies no
   default to any item.
precedent.why: Exact environment-field names and the encoded syntax and field-level validity rules of configuration values are State 6 contract details.

topics.topic: Expiry-pass initial timing, recurring schedule, missed passes, and lock scope
questions: When is the first pass, and how are later passes scheduled when a pass lasts beyond its nominal interval?
Does one pass hold the import lock while it visits all sessions, or release and reacquire it separately for each session?
When is the first expiry pass made?

Is the first pass at process start or 60 seconds later; are later passes on a fixed cadence or 60 seconds after completion; are missed or blocked passes queued, skipped, or coalesced; and is the import lock held for the whole traversal or reacquired for each session?

judgement.why: The same question about the cleanup pass's first run, cadence, delays, overlap and implementation scheduling was already judged non-observable on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Cleanup-pass first-run, cadence, delay, overlap, and catch-up rules
quotes:
Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.

A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check.
precedent.why: The limits themselves determine request refusal exactly, so the first tick, delayed-tick policy and overlap handling affect only internal reclamation of already inaccessible session state.

topics.topic: Monotonic session deadlines and their relationship to recorded UTC expiry
questions: What monotonic-clock facts or deadlines does an OwnerSession retain so that its limits can be enforced without deriving them from wall-clock instants?
What monotonic facts or deadlines does M11 carry so that session, idle, confirmation, and lockout limits can be decided without deriving them from the UTC instants?
What UTC instant is stored as the session's latest expiry, and what happens to that recorded fact when the wall clock changes while the actual deadline remains monotonic?

quotes:
Every duration in this decision — the 8 hours, the 30, 15 and 10
   minutes, the 60 seconds — is measured by the process's monotonic clock,
   which a change of the wall clock does not move; instants Registry records
   and the 03:00 of A18 are UTC wall-clock time.
judgement.why: The texts fix observable duration enforcement to the process's monotonic clock, while the private monotonic anchors or deadlines used to implement it and the wall-clock representation of an undisclosed session fact do not change any caller, owner or service behaviour.

topics.topic: Validity and stable resolution base of relative store and backup paths
questions: Are relative store or backup paths refused, or, if accepted, relative to which stable directory are they made absolute?
Are relative store or backup locations valid, and if so, relative to what stable directory?
Must configured locations already be absolute, or are relative paths resolved against some directory; and what directory is used if relative paths are allowed?

judgement.why: The same question about accepting and resolving relative configuration paths was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Resolution and canonicalization of relative configuration paths
quotes:
The store and the
   backup location are different places, neither inside the other, compared
   by their absolute paths with every symbolic link resolved — for a store
   file that does not exist yet, its directory resolved and its name added; a
   path that cannot be resolved, a broken link or a loop included, fails the
   start; a configuration
   where they are the same or one holds the other fails the start.
precedent.why: Whether relative path strings are accepted and the base used to interpret them are configuration-field syntax and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Whether suspended-host time advances session, confirmation, lockout, and pass timers
questions: Does elapsed session, confirmation and lockout time include time while the host or VM is suspended?
Must session, confirmation, and lockout durations advance while the host is suspended without restarting the process?
Does time while the host or VM is suspended count toward session expiry, confirmation expiry, lockout, and the 60-second pass interval?

quotes:
Every duration in this decision — the 8 hours, the 30, 15 and 10
   minutes, the 60 seconds — is measured by the process's monotonic clock,
   which a change of the wall clock does not move; instants Registry records
   and the 03:00 of A18 are UTC wall-clock time.
judgement.divergence: One implementation uses a monotonic clock that excludes suspended-host time, so sessions, confirmations and lockouts retain their remaining duration after resume; another uses a monotonic clock that includes suspended-host time, so they may already be expired after resume, which the owner notices through accepted versus refused requests and sign-ins.
judgement.why: The named monotonic clock does not determine whether time spent suspended advances the refusal deadlines.

topics.topic: Byte encoding, length, equality, and allowed characters for configuration secrets
questions: Which byte representation is used for the 32-byte test, constant-time comparison, and distinctness check?
How are environment-variable text values converted to bytes for length, equality, storage, and constant-time comparison, and are Unicode normalization or encoded NUL and newline values allowed?

judgement.why: The same question about secret text decoding, byte length, normalization and equality was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Secret and backup-key text decoding, byte length, normalization, and comparison
quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.

A presented secret is compared in constant time; no secret enters a record,
   a log line, an audit entry, a diagnostic or an answer (R0-23, R0-37).
precedent.why: The textual or binary representation, decoding, equality and byte-counting rules for credential fields are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: New-store temporary suffix and filename-collision prevention
questions: What exact suffix does the release declare, and what collision rule applies if the real store name itself already ends with that suffix?
What suffix does the release declare, and what prevents it from colliding with an existing user or Registry file that startup would otherwise remove?

judgement.why: The same question about the temporary new-store suffix, filename derivation and collisions was already assigned to State 6 on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Temporary new-store filename suffix, path derivation, and collision handling
quotes:
When the store's
   configured file does not exist and its directory does, Registry makes a new,
   empty store of the running release's version there at the start, under a
   temporary name — the store's name with a suffix the release declares —
   that it renames to the store's name only once the store is complete;
precedent.why: The suffix, filename derivation and representation of the temporary store path are filename-format and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Revalidation and handling of previously kept backups that later become corrupt
questions: Is consistency guaranteed only when a backup is first kept, or must later runs revalidate existing kept backups so corruption after creation cannot leave an inconsistent file counted and shown as a kept backup?
How must Registry handle an older kept backup whose header remains readable but whose encrypted store is corrupt or has been altered after its creation check?

quotes:
Registry decrypts a backup only to check it when it is made
   (rule 4); decrypting an older one, with the key it was made with, is part
   of a restore, outside Registry (rule 8, R0-89).

Third, whatever the second step did, it deletes every kept
   backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before the instant this step starts,
   one cutoff for the whole step, and every file under the kept
   prefix whose unencrypted record (rule 1) cannot be read.
a kept file's record is valid when its instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be read, and only a valid one counts as a kept backup;
judgement.why: Registry checks a backup's encrypted store only when making it; later runs retain an older backup while its unencrypted record remains readable, leaving decryption of that older copy to an external restore.

topics.topic: Whether an overlapping backup run permanently skips the next eligible date
questions: If the preceding backup is still running at the first eligible look for a new date, is that date permanently missed or should its run start later after the prior run finishes?
When the first qualifying clock look for a date finds the previous run still active, is that date permanently missed, or may its run start at a later look after the previous run finishes?

quotes:
a date's
   run starts at its first look at or after 03:00 of that date when an
   earlier look of the same process saw that date before 03:00, and no kept
   backup of that date exists

Runs
   never overlap: a 03:00 that finds a run still going makes no run of its
   own.
judgement.why: Only the date's first qualifying look can start its run, and if that look finds another run active the date makes no run of its own, so it is skipped rather than started later.

questions: What polling cadence and phase must implementations use, especially around starts, scheduler delays and wall-clock jumps?

topics.topic: Cleanup requirements when failed new-store creation leaves an unremovable temporary file
questions: If creating, checking, or renaming a new store fails and its temporary store file cannot be removed, may the failed start leave that file, despite the stated probe-only exception?

topics.topic: Coordination of concurrent Registry processes using the same installation
questions: What happens when a second Registry process starts against the same store or backup location?

topics.topic: Exact request-completion point for releasing import and session locks
questions: At what exact point is an upload, mapping, confirmation, import or sign-out request 'done' for releasing the import and session locks?

topics.topic: Locking order when an import clears uploads owned by other sessions
questions: When an accepted import clears uploads belonging to other sessions, must it acquire those sessions' locks, and if so in what deterministic order and for how long?

topics.topic: Startup behavior when a stale store temporary file cannot be removed
questions: If the real store exists but the stale temporary store file cannot be removed, does Registry fail the start or continue serving with the real store?

topics.topic: Whether expiry ends a session immediately or only when cleanup removes it
questions: At a limit, is the session already ended with cleanup merely deferred, or is it an expired but still existing session until the pass removes it?
